provenance.paper_title: From Verbatim to Gist: Distilling Pyramidal Multimodal Memory via Semantic Information Bottleneck for Long-Horizon Video Agents

evidence.paraphrase: The Sensory Buffer retains verbatim traces.
The pyramid distills sensory traces into episodes and gist.
During operation, MM-Mem applies a trained but frozen update module to fine-grained perceptual traces; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.
A fixed pyramid summarizes verbatim traces. For MM-Mem, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of fine-grained perceptual traces.
The information bottleneck abstracts task-relevant gist. For MM-Mem, this specifically supports abstraction of episodes into reusable experience of fine-grained perceptual traces.
Information moves through sensory, episodic, and symbolic tiers. For MM-Mem, this specifically supports migration between memory tiers of fine-grained perceptual traces.
During operation, MM-Mem applies merging or deduplication of overlapping entries to fine-grained perceptual traces; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

derived.hybrid_relation: Distinct operative representation paths are explicitly linked for downstream retrieval, reasoning, or control.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 3): The ADD/MERGE/DISCARD manager is trained offline and frozen at inference. It still changes memory content under a fixed policy, making the system T2. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
